name: Confluent Cloud
sku: Confluent Cloud with the Stream Governance Essentials package, included free. Stream Governance Advanced (data quality rules, business metadata, 7-day lineage vs 10-minute) is a separate paid add-on and not scored.

source.event-stream.note: A fully managed, cloud-native Apache Kafka engine on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure: elastic, partitioned, append-only topics producers publish to.

ingest.stream-ingest.note: Managed Kafka topics take continuous writes from producers, with many consumers reading the same topic independently.

transform.stream-processing.note: ksqlDB (SQL directly against topics) and a managed Apache Flink offering (SQL or Table API, stateful and low-latency) are both available as separately metered compute on top of the same topics.

bands.note: Confluent's own docs call this feature "data contracts": Schema Registry centralises, versions and enforces schema compatibility (Avro, JSON Schema or Protobuf) across topics, rejecting an incompatible change. Included free in Stream Governance Essentials, up to 100 schemas; Stream Governance Advanced adds Data Rules for richer enforcement on top of this.

Stream Catalog, part of Stream Governance Essentials, inventories topics and schemas with tagging and a self-service Data Portal. Business metadata and a GraphQL catalog API need Stream Governance Advanced.

Stream Lineage visualises how topics, connectors and stream processors relate. Included in Essentials but limited to the last 10 minutes of point-in-time data; Stream Governance Advanced extends it to 7 days.

A topic's retention period is a native, per-topic setting (retention.ms), 7 days by default and configurable down or up to infinite. A single retention lever, not the fuller residency or classification policy a governance platform manages.
Metrics on throughput, consumer lag and cluster health, with alerting.

presentation.tagline: Fully managed, multi-cloud Kafka with schema, catalog and lineage governance built in.

cost.note: The Basic cluster tier starts at $0/month base, with usage (ingress, egress, storage) billed on top; low, occasional volume stays cheap.
A Standard cluster starts at $385/month base and, per third-party estimate, handles most production workloads for a small team (around 5 engineers) at $500-800/month including usage.
An Enterprise cluster starts at $895/month base, plus higher ingress/egress/storage and per-feature meters (connectors, ksqlDB, Schema Registry, Stream Governance) at real volume.
